customer_updates.name: Tushar Thakur
customer_updates.text:
Live to Eat or Eat to Live which category you fall in. I definitely fall in live to eat whereas, its important that you eat to live for a healthy life.

If you are someone who knows me, I love to explore places and small food joints. I appreciate people who put up a small food business.Risks and business are fun for entrepreneurs. Meet my friend Jordan Lee aka Akash. I met him at a small place near my office, that place is now my favourite place for momos . Its located next to Carter blue at chincoli bunder near 5d. My friend makes  absolutely amazing momos, peri peri momos, thupka momos and chilli momos . Happiness is visiting his cart and having a conversation over wonderful momos. I have been requesting him to start a restaurant. Unfortunately, my friend couldn't get a place and neither I could find one within my contacts. His entire family is managing food business. One fine day, he shared about getting a place and opening a restaurant at Malad. This got me pumped and I congratulated him for his future endeavours. Flash forward, here I am at his restaurant trying couple of dishes. After shift, I went to his restaurant near jankalyan at Malad. To locate it wasnt that difficult google maps took me at the exact location(Mow Chow). We entered the beautiful place wit stunning lights, bright red interior and a great background music to soothen my mind. I felt calm with the surroundings and the vibe of the place.

Food :- I had ordered two dishes, one Chilli Basil Chicken as a starter and Chicken Triple Schezwan as main course. I wanted to try something simple and a dish I never tried before. Although, I regret I couldnt tried Chicken chilli which is my favourite. I will try next time for sure. The Chilli Basil Chicken had a soft texture inside and a crispy covering. It melted in mouth and had an authentic chinese taste. The spring onions,capisum and basil were nicely chopped, tossed and fried till they flavour the chicken. The taste was absolutely amazing and with every bite I enjoyed experience. The Chicken Triple Schezwan was off the hook. I dont like colors in my Triple Rice and always wanted it to be that way. I prefered a mix of nice noodles with more rice. Im so glad Chef Jordan, made it the same way that I like. It had that perfect amount of spice and chilli flakes to give it a perfect spice hit. I love the little extra eggs and menced chicken for a wonderful flavour. It was the dish of the day. The quality over quantity is something that I adored. I will visit this wonderful place with my office buds.

Conclusion: If you work,live or visit Malad do try this place. Its cozy, economical on budget and a true chinese experience. I love the interiors, plates and the serving concept. If uou are wish to experience true Chinese, North east cusines or amazing bao do visit this place. Its always good to see your friends grow and do great in life. I will visit this wonderful place with some friends to relish wonderful cusines , bao and dumplings. Until next time....

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
In a neighbourhood where Indo-Chinese kitchens often fluctuate between overly greasy and underwhelming, Stir Fry Grill has managed to maintain a steady standard for years. We’ve been ordering from and dining here for a long time now, and what keeps us returning isn’t hype — it’s consistency. The flavours remain reliable, the portions generous, and the pricing reasonable, which is increasingly rare in the Malad area.

What truly stands out is how well they balance quantity with quality. The food doesn’t try to be experimental or overly refined; instead, it focuses on delivering bold, satisfying Oriental flavours that work every single time.

Our regular staples include the Chicken Triple Rice, hearty and filling with properly spiced gravy; the Nasi Goreng, aromatic and flavour-packed; the Malaysian Flat Noodles, carrying that pleasant smoky wok finish; and the always dependable Crispy Chicken, which lives up to its name with a satisfying crunch.

Their starters have consistently impressed over the years. The Chicken Lollipop (dry) and Chicken 65 are flavourful and well-portioned. The Chilli Chicken (Dry) and Dragon Chicken deliver that classic spicy-tangy Indo-Chinese kick. Even vegetarian favourites like Veg Crispy, Paneer Chilli (Dry), and Veg Manchurian (Dry) are executed thoughtfully. Seafood options such as Prawns Chilli and Prawns Pepper Garlic add a richer dimension to the menu.

For rice and noodles, reliability continues with Schezwan Fried Rice, Burnt Garlic Fried Rice, and Combination Fried Rice — well seasoned without excessive oil. The Hong Kong Noodles and Schezwan Hakka Noodles are dependable comfort choices. Gravies like Chicken Manchurian, Hot Garlic Chicken, and Schezwan Chicken pair perfectly with these bases. Slightly different offerings such as Thai Green Curry (Chicken) and Veg Thai Curry with Rice are pleasantly balanced and not overly heavy. And when in the mood for nostalgia, the American Chopsuey delivers that familiar sweet-spicy crunch.

Over the years, what has mattered most is not a single standout dish but the steady benchmark they maintain. In an area where Oriental cuisine quality can be inconsistent, Stir Fry Grill continues to offer dependable flavours, satisfying portions, and honest pricing. It comfortably earns an above-average rating — not for flash, but for reliability, which is often far more valuable.

Flavours of China offers a delightful dining experience that lives up to its name. The restaurant's vibrant ambiance and comfortable seating make it a perfect spot if you want to experience desi chinese.

The dishes served were flavorful and well-presented. The Foc Lollypop Masala Dry was a standout, offering a perfect balance of spice and texture. It was served in green chatney which was unique to this restaurant. The Chicken Oriental Noodles were another highlight, with a rich, aromatic flavor containing flat noodles and exotic Veges with a kick of spiciness to it. The mocktails , including the Black Tart and Oceanic Orange, were refreshing and rounded off the meal beautifully.

The service was prompt and courteous, and the staff ensured a smooth dining experience. The pricing, considering the portion sizes and quality, was reasonable and value for money.

Overall, Flavours of China is a must-visit for Desi Chinese cuisine lovers seeking a comfortable dining experience. Recommended for its food and service.

I went here for a weekday dinner and the place got packed around 9PM. The kitchen service was smooth and dishes came on time. The table service by Staff Rahan was perfect as he was attentive. Special mention to Manager Ganesh as honestly he was among the few managers that I came accross who were very professional and polite plus fully committed to their job. He knew the menu well and he suggested grest options for us. And he single handedly was taking care of all the tables.

What We Had -
APPETIZERS~
Malaysian Chicken -
Sliced chicken done in peanut based creamy sauce tasted delicious. Loved the juiciness of the chicken and the peanut sauce had a hint of chilli in it hence you don't feel too much of peanuts in this.

Chicken Lollypop Schezwan Dry -
Huge lollypops done in schezwan sauce tasted outstanding. The size of the lollypops and the meat on it was marvellous. The sauce again had load of garlic in it still not to overpowering. A must try for lollypop lovers.

MAINS~
Chicken Oriental Noodles -
Flat noodles with exotic veggies, chicken and egg tasted good. Didn't had too much of spices  but taste wise it wasn't bland and had nice taste due to the multiple ingredients in it.

Chicken Five Spice Fried Rice -
Aromatic five spice done in fried rice with chicken and veggies tasted great. Loved the taste of the five spice as it doesn't taste like the normal fried rice.

DESSERTS~
Loconuts Ice Cream Roll -
Chocolate ice cream, almonds, brownie and chocolate sauce tasted heavenly. A great end to a perfect meal.

MOCKTAILS~
Oceanic Orange.
Grey Mango.
Both the drinks were nicely made with perfect ratio of syrup and soda hence perfect.

So the meal at Flavours of China was excellent from start to end as the food taste excellent, the service is great and the ambiance is nice. Hence this place should not be missed.

featured_reviews.name: Ankeeta
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Asia Kitchen for a family dinner and the entire experience was absolutely beautiful from start to finish. The moment we entered, the staff welcomed us so warmly that we instantly felt comfortable. The hospitality here is truly top tier — polite, attentive and genuinely caring throughout the evening.
The ambience deserves a special mention. The decor is superb, elegant and thoughtfully designed. The lighting, interiors and overall vibe make the place feel premium yet cozy at the same time. Everything around us looked stunning and beautifully maintained, making it perfect for a relaxed family dinner.
Coming to the food — Asia Kitchen serves authentic flavors that really stand out. We started with comforting bowls of Veg Eight Treasure soup, which was rich, flavorful and the perfect beginning to the meal. For dim sum, we tried the Truffle & Edamame dumplings and the Blue Pea & Spicy Asparagus dumplings, and both were incredibly fresh, delicate and packed with taste.
The small plates were equally impressive. The Crispy Chilli Corn and Cottage Cheese Chilli Oil with Spring Onion had the perfect balance of spice and crunch. For mains, we enjoyed Stir Fried Asian Greens with Tofu and Exotic Vegetables in House Smoked Chilli Sauce, both cooked beautifully with authentic seasoning and fresh ingredients.
The noodles and rice were comforting and satisfying — the Hakka Noodles and Blue Japanese Fried Rice with Vegetables & Edamame paired perfectly with the mains. We ended the meal on a sweet note with Honey Noodles with Almond Flakes, which was light, crunchy and absolutely delicious.
What truly elevated the evening was the staff. They checked in at the right moments, guided us through the menu and made sure we were taken care of without being intrusive. Their warmth added so much to the experience.
Overall, everything about Asia Kitchen — the hospitality, the staff, the ambience, the decor and the authentic food — came together perfectly. A dinner that felt special, comforting and memorable. Definitely a place we’d love to revisit with family again.

featured_reviews.name: SGT Reviews
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐ First Impressions & Location

Asia Kitchen sits on the first floor of Infiniti Mall 2, Malad, tucked beside the main food court walkway. Easy to spot, hard to ignore
that neon signage practically screams “Asian feast incoming”.
Ambience? Clean, modern, and very “pan-Asian chic”.

But let’s get to our experience… because the evening was a bit of a rollercoaster.

🍽️ What We Ordered

We went with a mix of classics and comfort bowls:
1. Papaya Salad (Som Tam)
2. Paneer & Chilli Peanut Starter
3. Ramen Bowl
4. Khow Suey
…and here’s where the plot twist enters.

⏱️ Service & Sequencing – The First Red Flag
Before our forks even warmed up, the main course arrived before the appetizer.
Yes… the Ramen Bowl lands first. Then the salad. Then the starter.
It felt like the kitchen was running its own maze without a map.

A small but important detail sequence matters, especially when flavours build on each other.

🍜 The Food — Ranked Best to Worst

1️⃣ Khow Suey – The Undisputed Winner

Creamy, fragrant, balanced, and comforting.
This bowl carried the whole dinner on its back like a Sherpa on Everest.
Perfectly cooked noodles, well-rounded curry broth, and toppings that actually made sense.

2️⃣ Papaya Salad – Crunchy, Fresh & Punchy
Bright flavours, generous peanuts, nice tang.
It’s the palate cleanser you want in an Asian meal, not the afterthought you sometimes get.

3️⃣ Paneer & Chilli Peanut Starter – Decent, Not a Showstopper
Paneer was soft, the peanuts added texture, and the chillies brought heat
but overall, this sat comfortably in the “good, not great” category.

4️⃣ Ramen Bowl – The Problem Child
This one hurt.
The broth? Tasteless.
Temperature? Lukewarm.
We actually had to ask them to reheat it  and even then, it didn’t redeem itself.
For a place that charges premium pricing, a flat ramen bowl is like missing a free throw in front of an open basket.

👨‍🍳 Staff & Experience

Service was polite but the timing issue made the whole meal feel disjointed.
They were courteous when we asked for reheating, but the kitchen clearly needs better coordination.

💸 Value for Money

The ambience and plating say “premium”.
But the portion-to-price ratio + service glitch makes it feel slightly overpriced unless you already love Mainland China’s flavour profile.

🎯 Final Verdict – SGT Scorecard

Ambience: ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Food (Overall): ⭐⭐⭐

Service: ⭐⭐½

Value: ⭐⭐½

Must-Order: Khow Suey

Skip: Ramen Bowl

Final Take:
A good spot for a mall lunch/dinner if you stick to their strengths.
But the service sequencing and the underwhelming ramen definitely took away some of the charm.
Go for the Khow Suey… the rest is optional.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Asia Kitchen by Mainland China offers a vibrant, semi-casual dining experience that does justice to pan-Asian flavours. From the moment you enter, you’re greeted with warm hospitality, a clean, upbeat ambience, and thoughtful interiors that let the food take centre stage. The variety is impressive — the menu spans Chinese staples, Thai curries, Japanese-style sushi and dim sums, even touches of Korean and Burmese cuisine.  Many dishes deliver in taste and presentation. Standouts  dishes are Crispy Lotus Stem, Avocado cream cheese sushi, Asparagus Cheung fun, Blue Pea Rice, Spicy Cottage Cheese and Vegetable Claypot and the dessert “Chocolate Dome.”  The lunch set / buffet options tend to offer good value, especially during off-peak hours.

If you’re looking for a place that’s more refined than street‐side Chinese, but not overly formal, this is a smart pick. It strikes a nice balance between flavour, variety, and ambience. A great option for dinners with friends, families, or when you want a slightly elevated Asian meal.
